rejected.why_rejected: It is the faithful archive of a SUPERSEDED generation: matrix_results_holo ran 2026-08-11 against a 3,610-molecule cached library, so its three ADMET bounds are that smaller library's min/max. Its own manifest declares its hypervolume NOT comparable to the preceding sweep. It reproduces NO archived history.csv.

clipping_under_canonical_bounds.measured_over: 53 archived runs, 4165 pooled rows (2437 distinct objective tuples)
hazards: hDHFR_Docking: 79 of 4061 pooled finite rows saturate at exactly 1.0. 15 of those are POSITIVE Vina scores (up to +10.73 kcal/mol) - physically non-binding/clashing poses - and because hDHFR is maximize ('want weak human binding') they all normalize to exactly 1.0, i.e. a FAILED dock scores as a PERFECT selectivity result. This is a scientific hazard in the frame, independent of which bound set is chosen.
PfDHFR_Docking: 18 of 4061 pooled finite rows clip to exactly 0.0 (score > -5, weaker than DOCKING_KCAL_MAX) and 18 saturate at exactly 1.0 (score < -11, stronger than DOCKING_KCAL_MIN).

Half_Life_hours: 6 pooled rows exceed the library max 64.849 (observed up to 81.633) and saturate at exactly 1.0. These are densified analogs whose ADMET-oracle prediction escapes the library-derived cube. loop._warn_if_docking_saturates warns for docking only; ADMET saturation is NOT warned.

Half_Life_hours: exactly 1 pooled row normalizes to 0.0 for a FLOAT ROUND-TRIP reason, not a scientific one: the library-minimum molecule is stored in evaluated.csv as 0.3763003051280975 while the bound is 0.37630030512809753, i.e. 5.551115123125783e-17 BELOW the bound, so it clips. Any reimplementation must expect CSV-serialized values to straddle a bound that was derived from a float32 artifact.
hERG_Toxicity_Prob and Caco2_logPapp: ZERO pooled rows clip at either end.

notes: These bounds define the normalized [0,1] maximization frame in which EVERY hypervolume in this project is computed; the reference point is the all-zeros corner (evaluation.fixed_reference_point).
The two docking bounds are FIXED CONSTANTS (raw kcal/mol), not data-derived; only the three ADMET bounds come from the library.
The numpy reimplementation must read these frozen numbers rather than recompute them, so a future library change cannot silently move the frame.
